title: FCA Annual Report Credits an International Finfluencer Crackdown With 3 Arrests and 650 Takedown Requests, as Insider-Dealing Cases Bring 11 Years in Prison Combined
summary: The FCA's Annual Report and Accounts 2025/26, published July 9, 2026, describes a nine-regulator finfluencer week of action that produced 3 arrests, 6 criminal proceedings, 11 warning letters, 50 warning list alerts and 650 social media takedown requests, alongside 17 criminal convictions, £1.77 million of market abuse fines and 2,329 scam warnings.
description:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority published its Annual Report and Accounts for 2025/26 and an accompanying press release on July 9, 2026; the web page's metadata lists July 8 as its creation date. The report covers the first year of the FCA's five-year strategy. This article uses the press release. Its headline numbers are the FCA's own claims, and the press release summarises the report rather than reproducing it, so readers who want the methodology behind estimates such as the £5.6 billion benefit figure should consult the annual report itself. The finfluencer action described below took place in June 2025, within the year the report covers.

The finfluencer week of action

Finfluencers are social media personalities who promote financial products or services. In the UK, financial promotions generally must be made or approved by an authorised firm, and a promotion by an unauthorised person can be illegal. According to the press release, the FCA led a week of action in June 2025 in which nine international regulators took part. The results it reports are:

3 arrests;
6 criminal proceedings;
11 targeted warning or cease-and-desist letters;
50 warning list alerts; and
650 requests to social media platforms to take content down.

The release does not say how many of the takedown requests led to content being removed, who was arrested or what the proceedings concern, so this article does not go further. Calculated here, the numbers show that most of the activity was on the content side: 650 takedown requests against 3 arrests.

Insider dealing, fraud and money laundering

The press release headlines insider dealing, saying that two cases secured a combined 11 years in prison. It describes the sentences as covering insider dealing and money laundering. Across the year, the FCA reports 17 criminal convictions, including for fraud, insider dealing, money laundering and offences under the Data Protection Act. It also reports that 12 individuals were fined a combined £1.77 million for market abuse. Dividing, calculated here, gives an average of about £148,000 per individual, though the release does not give the individual amounts, so the average hides large variation.

Firms were also penalised. The FCA fined firms about £14.4 million for transaction reporting failures and control weaknesses, and it fined Barclays £42 million for anti-money-laundering failures. The FCA reports that customers removed as money mules rose 4.4% to 222,173, across 35 firms.

Warnings

The FCA issued 2,329 warnings about unauthorised or potentially scam firms in 2025, up from 2,240 in 2024, an increase of about 4% calculated here. Its Firm Checker tool, launched in January 2025, has been used more than 1.9 million times. The release says firm warning messages protected an average of 694 consumers each week, a 49% increase after a 2026 advertising campaign.

Other claims in the report

The press release lists other results. The FCA estimates that its work delivered £5.6 billion in benefits to consumers, firms and the wider economy. It estimates that Consumer Duty fair-value rules will save people who pay insurance premiums monthly around £157 million a year. It says mortgage reforms are expected to let borrowers access up to £30,000 more, and that final rules on pensions and investments are expected to benefit at least 18 million consumers over the next decade. It reports that final Buy Now Pay Later rules were issued ahead of the regime starting in July 2026.

On growth and efficiency, the FCA reports nearly 50 pro-growth measures delivered in 2025, 132 applications to its AI-supercharged regulatory sandbox, two firms approved under the PISCES private markets framework with two more in the pipeline, new offices in the United States, Asia-Pacific and Singapore, and the retirement of outdated reporting returns, saving £16 million a year in reporting costs. It says AI automation cut handling time for simpler cases from up to four hours to about six minutes.

These are forward-looking estimates and self-reported efficiency figures, and the press release does not provide independent verification.

Quotes

FCA chair Ashley Alder said the regulator had made a strong start to its five-year strategy. Chief executive Nikhil Rathi said there was more to do but that this was a solid foundation.

What it means for consumers and creators

For consumers, the practical lessons are to check whether a firm is authorised using the FCA's Firm Checker, to be wary of financial tips on social media, and to check the FCA's warning list. For people who create financial content, the figures show that arrests and criminal proceedings are possible for illegal promotions, not only warnings. The release does not set out what promotions are permitted, and creators should check the FCA's financial promotion rules. This article is general information and not legal advice.
source_name: Financial Conduct Authority (press release: FCA cracks down on illegal promotions and market abuse in first year of new strategy, July 9, 2026)

key_points: The FCA published its Annual Report and Accounts 2025/26 on July 9, 2026, covering the first year of its five-year strategy, and estimates its work delivered £5.6 billion in benefits to consumers, firms and the wider economy.

The finfluencer 'week of action' in June 2025 involved nine international regulators and produced 3 arrests, 6 criminal proceedings, 11 targeted warning or cease-and-desist letters, 50 warning list alerts and 650 social media takedown requests.

The FCA secured 17 criminal convictions, including for fraud, insider dealing, money laundering and DPA offences, and two insider-dealing cases led to a combined 11 years in prison; 12 individuals were fined a combined £1.77 million for market abuse.
The FCA issued 2,329 warnings about unauthorised or potentially scam firms in 2025, up from 2,240 in 2024, and fined Barclays £42 million for anti-money-laundering failures.
The report also cites Firm Checker used over 1.9 million times, and the FCA's own estimate that Consumer Duty fair-value rules save monthly insurance premium payers about £157 million a year.
why_it_matters: Social media is now a main route by which younger investors meet financial products, and unauthorised promotions can lead to scams or unsuitable investments. The figures show how the FCA is using arrests, warning lists and takedowns alongside traditional enforcement, which tells consumers and influencers where the line is drawn.
